title: [Roadmap][Halo Ink 1/3] Ink v2 — pressure-aware stylus, eraser, palm rejection and resilient Canvas sketches
body:
## Standing roadmap — Stage 1 of 3: Halo Ink

**Status:** Source implementation committed on 2026-10-21; build, regression and physical qualification remain open. **Sequence:** Implement before Stage 2 (Ink as cognitive context) and Stage 3 (cross-device Ink). Not part of the current Android alpha stabilization gate.

### Goal
Turn Canvas sketches from a finger-drag prototype into a genuinely useful **device-independent pen input system** on Android, with progressive support for stylus/tablet capabilities. No mandatory Huion SDK or hardware purchase.

### Historical baseline before the 2026-10-21 source implementation
- `CanvasSketchEditor.kt` recorded drag positions using Compose `detectDragGestures`, with constant rendered stroke width.
- `CanvasSketchCodec.kt` persisted `sketch:v1|` with normalized integer X/Y only (64 strokes, 256 points/stroke); existing notes and sketches must keep working.
- `CanvasDrawingDraft.kt` and file markups provided a starting place for safe draft/recovery integration.
- Tablet model and input-hardware compatibility remain **unverified**.

### Scope
- [ ] Introduce a portable, bounded **InkStroke / InkPoint v2** domain model (normalized position, timestamp, pressure; optional tilt, orientation, tool type/eraser, buttons). Keep Android classes at the host boundary.
- [ ] Accept Android stylus `MotionEvent` data, including historical samples, pressure/tilt, hover and explicit eraser tool/buttons where available, while keeping smooth finger/mouse fallback.
- [ ] Perform palm rejection and tool arbitration without globally disabling touch or accessibility; distinguish drawing vs panning/zooming/selection.
- [ ] Render pressure-aware ink with appropriate smoothing, variable widths and stable transforms across tablet/phone density, orientation and zoom.
- [ ] Support erase (stroke and/or segment with well-defined semantics), undo/redo, predictable save/cancel, drafts/recovery after interruption.
- [ ] Increase reasonable bounded capacity without excessive allocations or serialized payloads; enforce quotas and safe handling of corrupted input.
- [ ] Define a versioned `Ink v2` codec and **v1 read compatibility**; no destructive migration and no loss of original sketch content.
- [ ] Adapt Canvas/PDF annotation surfaces for tablets: enlarged workspace, orientation, accessibility, keyboard/pen controls. Add EN/LV/RU text where UI changes require it.
- [ ] Keep the input abstraction vendor-neutral; Huion compatibility is an acceptance scenario, not a dependency.

### Acceptance criteria
- Finger sketches behave at least as they do today on phone-sized devices.
- Existing `sketch:v1` entries render/edit/save without loss. New v2 data round-trips with pressure/timestamps/eraser semantics intact.
- Stylus pressure and eraser work on an actual compatible pen device; unsupported attributes degrade correctly.
- Long sessions, rotation, process death/draft restoration, stylus disconnect/reconnect, palm contact and large drawings have bounded, tested behavior.
- Unit tests cover codec/versioning, geometry, normalization, quotas, undo/redo, and corruption; Android instrumentation tests cover pointer type/pressure/eraser and pen/finger fallback.
- No model/provider, Bluetooth, or proprietary-driver requirement to draw and save.

### Architectural guardrails
Android host collects pen events; portable runtime owns Ink state/format; Canvas/Study consume the same data model. Keep user data local, require explicit sharing for any remote inference, and distinguish *captured pen events* from *AI interpretation*.

### Out of scope
Handwriting recognition, AI understanding, cross-device syncing, and Huion-only SDK features belong to later tasks. Do not claim pressure/eraser support until physically verified.

## Source progress — 2026-10-21

Committed directly to `main`: [14b54b1d301ef4cf49b20c371c37e6ecf2d0cb9d](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/commit/14b54b1d301ef4cf49b20c371c37e6ecf2d0cb9d) (`[skip ci]`). Independent of the unpublished #40 search/media/cost package; no files from that package were applied.

Implementation and owner checklist: [`docs/engineering/HALO-INK-028-V2.md`](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/blob/14b54b1d301ef4cf49b20c371c37e6ecf2d0cb9d/docs/engineering/HALO-INK-028-V2.md).

### Implemented in source
- Portable SDK InkPoint/InkStroke/InkDocument, strict v2 codec with v1 read compatibility, per-contact transaction state, bounded undo/redo and swept whole-stroke erasure. Unchanged v1 is preserved without migration; unreadable data cannot be overwritten as an empty drawing.
- Android MotionEvent adapter: pointer-ID ownership, ordered historical samples, pressure normalized from advertised device range, optional tilt/orientation/buttons, hover, physical eraser/button, finger/primary-mouse fallback, stylus precedence and cancelled-contact rollback. Hardware behavior remains unqualified.
- Shared Compose editor for sketches and PDF/image overlays with pressure-width rendering, midpoint smoothing, separate draw/erase/pan modes, zoom/fit, keyboard undo/redo, accessible controls and expanded tablet layout. Original imported file bytes stay outside the write path.
- Existing completed-edit Room draft callbacks retained. In-progress/cancelled contacts are not persisted. PDF page/draft aggregate quotas are checked before accepting an edit; Cancel discards the recovery draft but does not modify saved content.
- 256 strokes, 2,048 points/stroke, 16,384 total points and a 262,144-character wire cap. Existing aggregate annotation/draft limits retained. Over-limit serialized edits roll back rather than truncate saved content.
- Preview/validation compatibility and all-version vector exclusion from plain-text search. Fifteen EN/RU/LV strings. No new permission, dependency, provider, vendor SDK, network flow or Room migration.

### Evidence and remaining gates
**17 files changed; 37 new test cases authored, NOT executed** (25 codec/edit/history/draft, 10 synthetic Android input, 2 search). Static source/call-site review, XML/key parity, whitespace and all 17 uploaded blob hashes checked; remote diff and `main` SHA read back. No Kotlin compilation, Gradle task, unit/instrumentation execution, CI/Actions, emulator or hardware validation was run.

**Keep this issue open.** Scope checkboxes above remain unqualified acceptance scope, not a claim that no source exists. Owner still needs build/regression results, a real compatible pen, finger/mouse checks, cancellation/palm behavior, large drawing performance, tablet/rotation/accessibility checks, and process-death/draft-write recovery. Undo history and viewport are session-local; recovery preserves completed document data. No specific Huion or other hardware compatibility is claimed.

## Verification update — 2026-10-22

At source revision `8045542df782bf6dba5b48b64e3188fd30dff35b`, `:app:testDebugUnitTest` passed 29 focused codec/editor tests and `:app:connectedDebugAndroidTest` passed 10 synthetic Android pointer-input tests on a Samsung SM-G990B2; the connected task assembled the APK. Details: [`docs/testing/HALO-INK-028-VERIFICATION-2026-10-22.md`](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/blob/dfc60e8a4fc0d2131c1a7106404b9488e345b1cc/docs/testing/HALO-INK-028-VERIFICATION-2026-10-22.md).

**Keep open.** These tests use synthetic events; no pressure-sensitive pen was used. Physical pen/eraser pressure, palm contact, tablet layout, rotation, process-death recovery, long-session performance, accessibility, and legacy sketch visual preservation are not yet qualified.

## Verified recovery, startup and cold-admission corrections — 2026-10-24

Published [3013a7ab5](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/commit/3013a7ab5d33ea9a799f7e9558a0e9b4bc7694b0) directly to main, fetch0/0 and clean checkout. [Report and raw evidence](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/blob/3013a7ab5d33ea9a799f7e9558a0e9b4bc7694b0/docs/testing/HALO-RECOVERY-INTENT-028-036-VERIFICATION-2026-10-24.md). Final focused gate9m17s:62 desktop cases (26 provider/36 app), zero failures/errors/skips;15 Python localization regressions,4796 PL resource coverage and exact prior EN/RU/LV/PL value/mapping parity pass. Both APKs assembled, installed package readbacks matched. Production app SHA83110b9e9313ff5748d96bc5670557f3e2555a2fcbeaf85f066faf8d561f07db; final fixture APK SHA38772c18a50d5897edf34629dfc022f1687ad3ae7762495014a737041c860b76. MainActivity resumed. No CI/Actions.

The preceding [508f4daa1](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/commit/508f4daa1a7f82b9f03de4724e71af945f049d81) fixed saving a valid fully erased existing sketch across UI/ViewModel/Room, while empty new sketches and corrupt data stay blocked. Current recovery now checks exact node/kind/original/file version before attachment. Save/Cancel cleanup uses the editor-observed receipt; Save also matches exact persisted sketch/pages payload. Transactional compare-and-clear retains unrelated, stale-source and newer same-source replacements, including replacements present before a save starts. Draft DB reads finish before copying current screen state. No new store/assistant operation. Keep OPEN: physical pen/palm/tablet, long sessions, full process-death/rotation/accessibility and original acceptance remain unqualified.

## Published code and current phone acceptance — 2026-10-24

Main [ee109c442](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/commit/ee109c442c455de57d78adf6187a300f9e0b4de4), fetched0/0 and clean checkout.

Canonical saved-sketch Clear now has a shared typed assistant operation with exact transactional board revision, local strictly valid Ink only, destructive ALWAYS approval/NEVER_REPLAY and durable changed/version receipts. It preserves card/aspect/links; rejects stale/corrupt/foreign/linked source writes; an open different-content stale editor/recovery cannot restore erased marks.33 grouped desktop/runtime cases and current native Canvas-owner clear/stale-readback case passed. [Source/installed hashes and raw evidence](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/blob/ee109c442c455de57d78adf6187a300f9e0b4de4/docs/testing/HALO-CANVAS-CLEAR-054-VERIFICATION-2026-10-24.md). **Keep OPEN:** real pressure pen/eraser/palm/tablet, broad process-death/accessibility/long-session qualification remain separate.

## Published equal-content drawing draft protection — 2026-10-24

Main [1e0d6cf9a](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/commit/1e0d6cf9a6573836609f3e0afc8812332271dd00), fetched divergence0/0 and clean checkout. [Source, phase-by-phase results, exact packages and raw evidence](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/blob/1e0d6cf9a6573836609f3e0afc8812332271dd00/docs/testing/HALO-DRAWING-RECEIPT-028-VERIFICATION-2026-10-24.md).

CanvasDrawingDraft now creates a UUID receipt per new editor emission and persists it in canvas-drawing:v2; existing transactional cleanup compares receipt plus all source/payload fields. Legacyv1 decoding remains deterministic without minting a new identity, and malformed/missingv2 IDs/unknown formats fail closed. Existing sketch/annotation callbacks already emit fresh snapshots; source-binding copies retain their receipt. No new store/Room migration/runtime/tool/approval owner, preferences, provider call or UI copy. This is snapshot identity, not a universal per-write or source-node revision/ABA protocol.

title: [Roadmap][Halo Ink 2/3] Ink as cognitive context — region selection, voice + drawing and Study annotations
body:
## Standing roadmap — Stage 2 of 3: Ink as cognitive context

**Status:** Planned / open backlog. **Depends on:** #28 (Halo Ink v2 portable strokes and stable drawing/annotation semantics). **Next:** Stage 3 cross-device Ink.

### Goal
Make handwriting, ink annotations and visually selected regions first-class **user-provided context** for Canvas, Notebook, Study and the cognitive runtime. Combine pen input with voice/text in a single interaction, without forcing all workflows through an AI provider.

### Core user journeys
1. Draw a diagram in Canvas, circle one part and ask: “Halo, explain this part.”
2. Annotate imported PDF pages or study worksheets, ask a question tied to the selected strokes/region, and get an answer anchored to the correct source/page.
3. Write a calculation or mark a student's answer; request **guided** Study feedback rather than automatically replacing the student's work.
4. Capture/annotate material on an Android tablet while a headset or glasses supplies the spoken instruction.
5. Keep strokes, source references and attached questions editable and retrievable in Notebook; no hidden one-off screenshot.

### Scope
- [ ] Implement a portable **InkSelectionContext** (stable workspace object / page identity; bounding region in document coordinates; selected stroke IDs; revision/version; origin and timestamps).
- [ ] Provide box/lasso or other accessible region selection, clear hover/selection affordance and an explicit **Ask about selection / Add to working set / Study this** UI entry point.
- [ ] Bind ink context to existing Canvas/Notebook source objects, PDF page geometry and annotations; preserve selection fidelity under zoom, rotation, edits and page changes.
- [ ] Extend the cognitive context/observation contract to include referenced region metadata and an optional privacy-controlled cropped render, with deterministic fallback when vision/OCR is unavailable.
- [ ] Support mixed voice + pen turns: strokes/selection establish referent; the speech transcript describes the instruction. Handle ambiguous/outdated selections with clarification, not inferred actions.
- [ ] Provide intent-specific flows in Study (question → attempt → hint → feedback → revision), keeping educational guidance separate from generating the answer outright.
- [ ] Make selection provenance, local/remote processing decision, model availability, action approvals and receipts inspectable; do not send handwriting/images to cloud providers without policy approval.
- [ ] Provide EN/LV/RU UI copy and appropriate handwriting/OCR limitations; no assumption that every language/script is supported by one recognizer.
- [ ] Ensure deterministic selection, attachments, context bookmarks and local markup work **without** AI.

### Acceptance criteria
- User can select a drawn region and ask about **that exact selection**; the answer is linked to source object/page/ink revision rather than an untracked screenshot.
- Selected strokes/page anchors remain valid through save/reopen, orientation changes and basic edits; stale/deleted references are explicitly rejected or repaired with user involvement.
- With an unavailable provider or denied cloud consent, strokes and selections remain locally usable, and AI-only operations report a truthful limitation.
- Mixed voice-and-ink referents are resolved from the same interaction session; conflicting or ambiguous referents require clarification.
- Tests cover selection geometry, stable IDs, source revisions, region cropping privacy, Study guided flow, transcription attachment and provider failure.
- Performance and memory stay bounded on a phone; tablet layout is practical.

### Architectural guardrails
Canonical Canvas and Notebook objects remain sources of truth; Ink is structured input and referenced context, **not** a separate hidden notes database. Use the existing runtime's context, permission, model/provider and journal boundaries. Avoid direct unrestricted system/screen access.

### Out of scope
Live cross-device transport, proprietary Huion APIs and general-purpose remote drawing controls are Stage 3. No automatic handwriting-recognition accuracy claims.


## Source progress — portable selection contract, 2026-10-22

Committed and pushed to main as [5263244795a89b9d910105a1f48d5300fecd3792](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/commit/5263244795a89b9d910105a1f48d5300fecd3792). Added versioned, platform-neutral selection bounds and a context carrying workspace/page identity, source revision, selected stroke references, gesture origin, and timestamps in `sdk/runtime-sdk/src/main/java/com/halo/sdk/runtime/ink/InkSelectionContext.kt`. Validation rejects malformed/oversized references, duplicate stroke IDs, zero-area or out-of-range regions, invalid timestamps, and unsupported schema versions.

Verification: test-first red check failed on the missing contract types as expected; focused test passed, then full `:sdk:runtime-sdk:test` passed. This is only a portable data contract. Existing InkStroke records do not yet provide stable IDs, and no Canvas selection UI, source binding, crops, cognitive context, Study flow, or physical acceptance landed. Keep #29 open.

## Exact Ink selection handoff — 2026-10-23

Published [8739c2a6cd67de457f131253bdb7f8573444e9fc](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/commit/8739c2a6cd67de457f131253bdb7f8573444e9fc) to main; fetched divergence 0/0. Existing selection/Ask/Study/working-set paths now reject a replaced or deselected bookmark, edited/deleted source, inactive imported file, unavailable/relinked file and changed file version. Exact source validation and synchronous visual-context publication share the canonical Room read transaction after suspending media preparation. Cancellation releases only the newly owned attachment/context reservations, including cancellation before a reference is delivered. Study rejects/trashes its own incomplete material after a stale handoff.

Production/regression source completed before validation; follow-up source review clear. **37 focused app cases passed on the first run**, zero failures/errors/skips; production and test compilation passed. [Verification and raw results](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/blob/8739c2a6cd67de457f131253bdb7f8573444e9fc/docs/testing/HALO-INK-SELECTION-029-VERIFICATION-2026-10-23.md). No APK assembly/install or physical acceptance in this batch (ADB absent).

**Keep open:** physical pen/tablet/palm qualification, actual spoken Ink referents and permitted provider flows remain unqualified. Existing stable stroke IDs, selection UI/bookmarks/crops and Study integration are already in source; the original #29 description predates them. Cross-device Ink remains #30. No CI/Actions run.

title: [Roadmap][Halo Ink 3/3] Cross-device Ink — tablet/desktop pen input into Halo sessions
body:
## Standing roadmap — Stage 3 of 3: Cross-device Ink

**Status:** Planned / open backlog. **Depends on:** #28 (portable Ink v2), #29 (Ink/context source-reference contracts). Implement once the local Android ink experience and alpha runtime stability are verified.

### Goal
Let an Android tablet, Windows/Linux drawing tablet or desktop pen surface act as an **input endpoint** for a Halo session hosted on another device (Android, HaloLinux/Pi, future wearables), using the ecosystem's canonical device/session architecture. Make this a general capability, **not a vendor-specific Huion integration**.

### Supported concepts / target journeys
- Android tablet runs Halo Ink UI while a separate HaloLinux/Pi or desktop node owns reasoning and tools.
- USB pen tablet on Windows/Linux enters ink through a native host adapter; Halo receives portable ink events rather than raw OS HID packets.
- User sketches or annotates on tablet while listening/speaking through HeyCyan/headphones; a single cognitive turn correlates *voice intent*, *selected region* and *session identity*.
- Connectivity interruption preserves local strokes; user can explicitly resume/sync without replaying external actions.

### Scope
- [ ] Define `InkEndpoint` and `InkSession` capabilities in the existing Runtime/SDK device registry; identify input, display and processing owners separately.
- [ ] Design a versioned `InkEventEnvelope` (source device, session/interaction ID, document/board ID, stroke IDs, sequence number, timestamps, revision, bounded payload). Do not pass Android `MotionEvent` across host boundaries.
- [ ] Implement secure opt-in discovery/pairing or explicit trusted-endpoint association through the existing DeviceSessionManager; prevent unauthenticated LAN/USB peers from injecting events.
- [ ] Establish encrypted transport/handshake compatible with local-first operation; no required vendor cloud or central backend. Reuse an existing Halo transport if it meets safety requirements rather than creating an independent socket protocol.
- [ ] Handle input jitter, pen-up/down order, dropped/repeated events, rate-limits and flow control. Separate ephemeral live preview from durable committed strokes.
- [ ] Add idempotent synchronization/checkpoint and explicit conflict/revision handling. Reconnection and process death **must not duplicate strokes or authorize any tool invocation**.
- [ ] Expose per-device input capabilities (pressure, tilt, eraser, hover, display geometry), observed status and connection lifecycle on the Devices page.
- [ ] Support Android stylus first, then Windows/Linux pen/HID adapters. Investigate OpenTabletDriver and Huion compatibility per exact model/OS/architecture; Pi 5 ARM64 compatibility is a test hypothesis, not a promise.
- [ ] Keep Ink-as-context and voice route bindings through the current CognitiveSession / Interaction ID boundaries; never infer permission to open unrelated apps from a pen event.
- [ ] Add explicit remote-session start/stop, session ownership, privacy/security diagnostics, accessible disconnect UI and deterministic fallback to local drawing.

### Acceptance criteria
- A paired Android tablet can draw into a remote Halo Canvas session; gestures and stroke data converge exactly once and remain editable across reconnection.
- Pressure/eraser values retain the correct meaning where the source hardware exposes them; unsupported hardware falls back gracefully.
- A voice command from one endpoint can refer to a region selected on another endpoint **only** when both belong to the same authorized interaction/session.
- Unauthorized/replayed/stale events are rejected; server-side access checks apply despite UI approval state.
- Disconnect, sleep, wake, process death, host restart and simultaneous edits have explicit observable outcomes and no silent data loss or replayed tool actions.
- Benchmarks and tests cover latency budget, sequencing, memory quotas, packet loss/duplication, authentication, sync conflict and battery use; run on a real Android tablet + at least one second host.
- Android/Windows/Linux platform capabilities have explicit compatibility records. Don't call Huion, Windows or Pi support complete without physical validation.

### Guardrails
Local-first and vendor-neutral. The tablet/pen is an **input modality**, not an authority escalation channel. Retain Halo's existing permissions, user approval, trace/journal, provider independence and canonical session boundaries.

### Out of scope
Direct remote HID control of another user's desktop, headless unrestricted shell/app commands, required cloud accounts, speculative OpenTabletDriver ARM64 support and shared-document multi-user collaboration.

title: Halo runtime: parallel voice pipeline, CPU/GPU orchestration and model residency
body:
## Context
Halo's current voice pipeline (STT → intent → model selection/reasoning → tools → TTS) incurs cumulative latency. On the test phone, some identical local LiteRT models generate **~2–3× slower on GPU than CPU**, while certain models take **4–6 minutes to load**. These are user observations, not standardized benchmarks. Goal: **parallelize independent stages and serialize dependent stages correctly**, rather than assuming GPU always wins.

## Proposed runtime design
- Represent each request as a cancellable, dependency-aware execution graph with stage events, deadlines, bounded queues and backpressure.
- Stream STT partial hypotheses on CPU; run lightweight deterministic command matching and optional intent classifier incrementally. Finalize intent only when confidence/utterance boundary permits; prevent premature device actions.
- In parallel, pre-load/warm the candidate reasoning model when useful; only dispatch finalized, authorized requests. GPU LLM is **optional**, selected by measured performance, not by assumption.
- Overlap retrieval/embedding and context preparation where independent; start streaming TTS on stable response chunks while generation continues, with interruption/barge-in and cancellation.
- Use structured tool execution for Notebook/Canvas (create/edit files, formatting, assets); embedding models support retrieval, not document editing. Require confirmations for consequential actions.
- Keep CPU, GPU, potentially NNAPI/NPU and cloud execution as independently selectable backends, subject to actual LiteRT support and device capability.

## Model roles / configuration
- Extend existing role assignments: STT, intent, embedding/retrieval, reasoning, tool selection, vision, TTS. Some roles may be rules or platform services rather than neural models.
- Decouple **role → candidate model** from **model → backend**; permit reuse of one model for several roles, prioritized fallback and explicit capability checks.
- First-run onboarding: automatically select a tested, downloadable default pack (no requirement to browse Hugging Face). Curate from models actually benchmarked on test devices, verify model format, provenance/license, checksum, disk/RAM requirements and compatibility.
- Advanced/Developer Settings: manual role/backend pinning, preloading/residency, tuning, profile presets, benchmark data and per-stage trace. Preserve simple consumer defaults.
- Residency manager: memory budget, load/unload policies, warmup, eviction under Android memory pressure, thermal throttling awareness. Do not prewarm every model.

## Benchmark and correctness plan
1. Inventory only models **already downloaded on the test phone**; do not download new models for initial benchmark.
2. For identical model/quantization/prompt/context/settings, measure cold/warm load, prefill tok/s, decode tok/s, time-to-first-token, peak RSS/memory, CPU/GPU utilization, thermal state and failures.
3. Confirm actual GPU delegate operation placement/fallback, quantized kernels, KV cache and synchronization overhead. A successful GPU init is not proof that the whole graph runs there.
4. Compare serial baseline vs concurrent pipeline by end-of-speech → first audio, full voice-to-voice latency, success rate, energy and thermal stability. Concurrent work may **regress** performance due to shared memory/bandwidth.
5. Test overlapping speech, interruptions, background/foreground, model eviction, device low-memory, BT audio/glasses disconnect and provider failures. Record trace IDs across EventBus, Orchestrator, Speech Runtime and ReasoningEngine.

## Implementation phases
- **P0:** instrumentation, reproducible ADB/device benchmark, trace timeline, existing downloaded model inventory.
- **P1:** stage DAG, safe streaming STT/intent, bounded concurrency, cancellation, CPU fast path.
- **P2:** adaptive residency and measured backend selection with manual overrides.
- **P3:** parallel retrieval + chunked streaming TTS; structured Notebook/Canvas tool routing.
- **P4:** curated one-click model packs and onboarding/developer UX (coordinate with ongoing DevKit v1.2 UI redesign).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] End-to-end traces show concurrent stages and real per-stage latency.
- [ ] Auto mode improves median/p95 end-of-speech-to-first-audio against measured baseline **without compromising correctness**; report regressions honestly.
- [ ] Manual CPU/GPU assignments and fallback work; unsupported GPU combinations are clearly rejected.
- [ ] Simple voice commands can bypass heavy LLM.
- [ ] Memory/thermal guardrails, cancellation, safe device actions and cloud privacy permissions covered.
- [ ] Existing local/cloud providers and onboarding remain functional.
- [ ] No GitHub Actions or CI; GitHub is code/issue storage only.

**Status:** architecture/backlog; no code changes authorized by this issue.

## Coordination update — 2026-10-19
- User-facing uninterrupted hands-free voice UX (explicit foreground session, no mic re-tap, barge-in, Supertonic/Kokoro playback, local/hybrid parity) is tracked separately in #38. This issue remains the existing DAG, concurrency, residency and benchmarking foundation; avoid duplicate audio engines.
- Verified model packs and role/device/language-specific catalog are tracked in #39; local/OpenRouter Free/specialist policy in #40.
- The product alpha quality gate is #43. Close #33 based on measured device performance and safe cancellation, not source commits alone.
- Architecture decision #41: no developer-operated remote voice, AI, agent or sync functional service; user-owned cloud providers called directly. Commerce-only server exception does not affect this voice runtime.


## Native speech admission cancellation — 2026-10-23

Published [ca93d4037ab2ed40de8b8bb53b354df2912d36d2](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/commit/ca93d4037ab2ed40de8b8bb53b354df2912d36d2) to main; fetched divergence 0/0. Supertonic now covers resource admission inside its existing cleanup; Kokoro no longer skips cleanup if admission is cancelled before returning success. Both preserve native teardown before resource release, the existing owner locks, successful warm/stream residency and output routing. No new engine or scheduler.

Source and regressions preceded validation; read-only review clear. **37 focused app cases passed on the first run**, zero failures/errors/skips (actual-provider admission cancellation 2, voice conversation 12, playback lifecycle 19, Supertonic pack ownership 4). The new cases use the real generic resource manager/coordinator and bounded fixture packs; admission is blocked before native initialization, then cancellation must release TTS compute while independent ASR residency survives. [Verification/raw evidence](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/blob/ca93d4037ab2ed40de8b8bb53b354df2912d36d2/docs/testing/HALO-SPEECH-ADMISSION-033-VERIFICATION-2026-10-23.md).

**Keep open:** no new physical baseline/concurrent latency, actual CPU/GPU placement, audio, power/thermal or permitted provider acceptance. No APK assembly/install; ADB and Windows device inventory currently show no Android phone. No CI/Actions run.

## Current phone native PCM smoke — 2026-10-23

Published [ca4c0e9d2](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/commit/ca4c0e9d298cd2316eae6fb24e489a1711c091fa) to main; fetched divergence0/0 and clean checkout. title: HALO-VOICE: hands-free continuous local/hybrid conversations and barge-in
body:
## Vision
One explicitly initiated Voice Mode session lets user speak naturally for multiple turns WITHOUT tapping a microphone for each utterance. Accessible from Home/Chat/Study/Notebook and future Screen, with same user experience for local/hybrid execution. Initial scope foreground session, NOT stealth always-on hotword/microphone.

## Flows
- Start → VAD/endpoint + STT (partial hypotheses for UX, final for actions) → local intent/tools → local or selected online LLM → chunked streaming Supertonic TTS (Kokoro fallback) → auto-listen for next turn.
- Immediate voice/touch stop, pause, mute, repeat, end; cancellation/barge-in interrupts TTS, LLM and stale callbacks; do not treat speaker echo as human command.
- Android audio focus, speaker vs headset/BT/glasses, echo suppression, lifecycle/process death, foreground permissions, visibility, accessibility and battery/thermal budget.
- Local profile targets 12GB+ when measured, optional 8GB lighter path; no RAM-only guarantees. Hybrid profile local audio/intent + direct BYO cloud reasoning, with informed consent and no silent transmission.
- Measure warm/cold audio latency, p50/p95 end-of-utterance to audible answer, memory, CPU/GPU, model residency, interruption success and energy; ~2s warm response is goal, not promise.
- Strict tool safety: never act on partial/ambiguous ASR, do not speak hidden markers, no stale audio and no duplicate actions.
## Acceptance
10+ turn conversation on real Android without mic re-tap; interruption works offline and during generation, switch model during playback safely; no false cloud use; honest missing-model/permission recovery.
## Dependencies
Extend existing #33 concurrent speech/residency and #36 local intent. Do NOT duplicate their implementations.
## Implementation discipline
- Start from current main, inspect existing components and BrandBook/DevKit, reuse runtime and Compose; no global rewrites.
- Keep internal traces/experimental model settings in Advanced → Development.

## Pricing/product decision — 2026-10-22
The base Halo app will be a paid Google Play listing, targeting approximately US $4.99 as a one-time purchase. No Halo monthly subscription. Third-party provider subscriptions/credits are the user's choice. Future major feature packs may be separately purchased once, but require a separate product and architecture decision.

## Base-app commerce architecture
The Play Store listing and the buyer's Google Play account handle app delivery, access, and purchase/refund records. Halo will not implement an in-app base-app unlock, purchase-token handling, entitlement cache, or commerce backend for the paid listing. Installation on a replacement device/reinstall must be checked against the same Play account through the actual store flow.

Google Play's paid-app refund and order-management flows apply. Provide a clear support contact and handle refund/access questions according to Play Console guidance and applicable law. Localized prices, taxes, countries/regions, support details, and availability must be set and reviewed in Play Console; $4.99 is a target, not a configured global price.

## Optional feature packs
No feature pack is currently approved or implemented. Do not ship service-account secrets in the APK. No assistant data, AI requests, notes, audio, provider credentials or behavioral analytics may enter commerce infrastructure. ## Alpha gates / user journeys
1. **Continuous voice:** on a physical Android phone, voice conversation for 10+ turns in supported languages with explicit session start, no repeated tap, stop/barge-in, offline/online state clarity; see #38 and #33.
2. **Safe ask → act → respond:** spoken/typed command goes through final ASR, local intent, authorized native/tool schema execution, clear result; no duplicates/wrong actions or tool markup in chat/TTS; see #36 and #40.

5. **Setup and recovery:** new user sees easy model/provider choices, first run without raw HF catalog, tested TTS/STT; reboot/process death/offline/permission denial/model removal error recovery, see #39 and #27 (historically closed).
6. **Privacy and ownership:** runtime functions operate device-local or direct BYO provider, never via developer functional servers; billing exception only as #41/#42. No hidden third-party request or surprise charge.

title: [P0][HALO-TOOLS-AI] All user-facing tools must be operable by Halo via voice and natural language
body:
## New universal engineering requirement · user decision 2026-10-22
**Every Halo capability exposed as a user-facing tool must be accessible through the same Halo assistant, in natural language by typing or speaking, to the extent technically possible and authorized by the user.** A tool is not 'complete' if it only has a button/UI and cannot be safely invoked or controlled by Halo. This is a **cross-cutting Definition of Done for future feature development**, not a new parallel agent runtime.

Examples: "Crop this image and save a copy", "Put the selected photo in my Canvas", "Create a note summarizing these documents", "Export the annotated PDF", "Show the result in Studio", "Find my earlier drawing and open it". Voice and text requests use the **same semantic operation and the same execution owner**. A complex workflow may chain multiple supported actions, with explicit status and only authorized side effects.

## Agent instructions
1. First inventory existing tools and owners against **`ToolRegistry`, `ToolDescriptor`, `CapabilityCatalogue`, `ToolDiscoveryService`, `PolicyToolAuthorizer`, `CognitiveSession`, `AgentStep` journal, existing host native actions/permissions**. Extend those owners, do not create another execution/approval engine.
2. Define an additive versioned **AI-operability contract** for every feature: capability ID; user-facing descriptions/discovery; typed argument and result schemas; read/query/list, create/edit/export/delete operations as applicable; supported modes/devices; actual availability and permissions; idempotency/replay policy; timeout/cancellation; undo/preview where meaningful; provenance and result receipts.
3. Register discoverable, actionable operations with the existing runtime at feature integration time, rather than exposing static tool-name suggestions. Tool UI and assistant invocation must converge on the **same use case/domain owner**, returning equivalent outcomes.
4. Assistant should resolve a named object/selection/source revision and clarify ambiguity. Ensure real STT-final intent -> safe typed plan -> authorization -> execution -> verified feedback. Do **not** execute guessed tool names, trust untrusted file/web text as instructions, treat model output as permission, or allow hallucinated success.
5. Existing Android permissions, Kids restrictions, Private/Power dispatch gates, scoped provider billing/limits and approval for consequential actions stay enforceable. Prefer one user-configured permission/policy over repetitive Halo 'Allow tool?' prompts for routine allowed actions; never bypass Android or external effect confirmations.
6. Both hands-free voice (#38) and ordinary chat (#44) discover/use these operations, including errors, cancellation, continuing long tasks and clear 'needs setup' / 'unavailable' states. Do not claim arbitrary cursor/pen gestures can be automated when only a human hand can perform them; expose meaningful document and tool operations.
7. Update **`.agents/AGENTS.md` / engineering review checklist** when implementing so every future feature must demonstrate assistant-callable functional parity (or document an explicit, justified hardware/security exception). Apply this rule retroactively to high-value existing tools and to new Studio/Workspace tools.
8. Keep tool status and user-facing presentation aligned with Home Tools catalog #45 and Orb #46; UI convenience wrappers are *not* separate execution systems.

## Acceptance / Definition of Done
- [ ] At least three real cross-tool workflows execute end-to-end by **typed request and by spoken request** with exactly the same saved objects/outcomes and truthful receipts, both on-device and permitted Power route.
- [ ] Agent cannot perform restricted/destructive/external actions without the existing required approval, and Private never silently sends content to cloud.
- [ ] Discoverability, typed validation, missing-capability/permission recovery, cancellation/interrupt, process death, source-version conflicts and duplicate/replay safety are demonstrated.
- [x] Add a reusable 'AI-controllable tool' verification template to the development workflow; missing it blocks declaring a newly shipped interactive tool complete.

## Distinction from existing issues
#36 qualifies current phone intent/tool correctness; #45 presents a discoverable user tool catalog; #38 owns voice lifecycle. **This issue establishes the permanent cross-project contract and closes gaps** among UI tools, capabilities and Halo’s assistant. Implement on the current runtime owners rather than duplicating their functionality.

## Mandatory repository principles for implementing agents
Read **[`.agents/AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/blob/main/.agents/AGENTS.md)**, current source architecture, **[`docs/15-brand/v4/IMPLEMENTATION.md`](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/blob/main/docs/15-brand/v4/IMPLEMENTATION.md)** and its `USER_FACING.md` before changes. Start from the latest `main`. Extend canonical owners, avoid duplicate stores/engines, keep Runtime platform-independent and Android specifics in Host. Local-first, privacy-safe Private/Power, no Halo-operated functional servers (#41). No new GitHub Actions/CI. Do not equate source completion with verified Android/device acceptance; report actual status and follow the repository's current execution/testing rules. Reuse [#36](https://github.com/slafftrosheen/Halo/issues/36) and current assistant action/runtime contracts; do not add UI-only tools.
